text:
ConocoPhillips fell 1.2% today, pulling back from a three-day rally that had pushed the stock to $142.28 on November 13th. The decline coincides with oil prices sliding slightly—U.S. crude dropped to $89.62 per barrel, down from the highs earlier in the week—which directly affects profitability for oil producers. The stock has given back about 4% over two weeks as energy prices have cooled.

The timing of today's pullback is notable given the Iran escalation news from yesterday (a third U.S. carrier in the Gulf, threats rising). That story briefly supported oil prices and energy stocks earlier in the week, but those geopolitical fears appear to have faded from traders' minds as the rally unwound. Rising heating oil prices and broader shipping-cost inflation signal economic pressure that could dampen fuel demand heading into winter, adding another headwind to the sector's near-term outlook.
